metadata.description: Single consolidated UK SOC 2020 dataset: occupation classification, every indexed job-title variant, and Skilled Worker sponsorship eligibility/going rates, all keyed by soc2020_code.

sources.name: ONS SOC 2020 Volume 2: The Coding Index
ONS SOC 2020 structural framework (major/sub-major/minor group titles)
Immigration Rules Appendix Immigration Salary List

corrections_applied: Excluded 231 ONS index rows whose SOC code was the literal placeholder '}}}}' (cross-reference-only entries with no direct code) — preserved separately under unresolved_cross_references instead of silently dropped.

Title field uses the majority/consistent title from the raw ONS coding index rather than the pre-existing compact file, which fixed 4 genuine discrepancies (codes 2212, 3131, 2122, 2236) including one character-encoding bug on 2236's apostrophe.

Category field verified against ONS SOC2020_framework.csv for all 412 codes; 344 matched exactly, 68 (all major group 3) differed only because the framework file uses an abbreviated label ('ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONAL OCCUPATIONS') — the fuller, widely-published official name ('Associate professional and technical occupations') was kept.

Sponsorship status distinguishes 4 states: eligible_standard_route, eligible_health_education_route, ineligible, and legacy_only_not_open_to_new_applicants (eligible only under pre-22-July-2025 rules, i.e. not for new hires) — all 412 codes classified, none left unclassified.

Codes 6131/6135/6136 carry an alternate_route_caveat: their real-world sponsorship route (Health and Care Worker visa) is governed by a separate document (Appendix Skilled Worker) not scraped for this dataset — flagged rather than mislabeled as ineligible/legacy.

merged_uk_soc_full_json.source_note: User-supplied file data/uk_soc_full.json (generatedAt 2026-07-14T17:52:38Z, dataSource effectiveDate 2026-07-01). Cross-verified against this dataset before merging.

verification_result.occupation_code_set: Identical 412 codes in both files — exact match.
verification_result.rate100_annual_salary_for_standard_route: 0 mismatches across all 91 codes — confirms both files derive the same Table 1 figures correctly.
verification_result.title_field: 47 cosmetic differences ('n.e.c.' vs 'not elsewhere classified.'), plus 3 genuine discrepancies (codes 2212, 3131, 2236) that exactly match bugs already found and fixed in this dataset using the raw ONS index — uk_soc_full.json appears to have been built from the same older, uncorrected compact source. This dataset's titles were kept as authoritative.
verification_result.eligibility_classification: 187 disagreements found. 10 were checked directly against the raw gov.uk Appendix Skilled Occupations HTML and confirmed as errors in uk_soc_full.json (codes it marked 'RQF6+ eligible' are actually on the official Table 6 ineligible list, with no salary data to back the claim). The remaining 177 disagreements are all codes this dataset classifies as legacy_only_not_open_to_new_applicants (Table 1a/3a, explicitly scoped by gov.uk to 'applicants granted permission under rules in place before 22 July 2025') that uk_soc_full.json marks simply 'eligible: true' without that distinction. Given the confirmed errors elsewhere in the same eligibility field, this dataset's verified 'sponsorship.status' was kept as authoritative; uk_soc_full.json's claim is preserved per-code under 'routes_per_uk_soc_full_json' for transparency, not used to override anything.

additive_data_merged: sponsorship.going_rate_gbm_scaleup_25th_percentile — Table 2 rates (Global Business Mobility / Scale-up routes), previously excluded as out of scope; added since it doesn't conflict with anything and may be useful.

sponsorship.national_pay_scale_bands — fully resolved NHS Agenda for Change band tables (England/Scotland/Wales/NI) nested directly per health/education occupation, replacing the raw 'see Table 4' text this dataset had before.
visaSalaryRules — the full points-options rule table (A-K: floor salary, going-rate percentage, and condition for each), kept at top level.

visaSalaryRules.note: Sponsor must pay whichever is higher: the flat floor salary below, or the going-rate percentage for the SOC code.
